title: Past Simple vs Present Perfect
summary: Choose a tense by deciding whether the time is finished or remains relevant now.
learningObjectives: Contrast finished past events and life experiences.
Use present perfect for a current result.

explanation.heading: Past simple
explanation.body: Use past simple for completed events located in a finished past period.
explanation.example: We repaired the server on Tuesday.

explanation.heading: Present perfect
explanation.body: Use have/has + past participle for experience or a present result when the event time is not specified.
explanation.example: I have repaired this kind of fault before.

explanation.heading: Time expressions
explanation.body: Finished periods often take past simple; so far, yet and ever commonly signal a present connection.
explanation.example: We completed three tests last week, and we have completed two so far this week.

right.label: Present perfect
right.note: No specific finished time is given.

examples.note: The loss happened at a specified finished time.

examples.sentence: Did you see the message this morning?
examples.note: Appropriate if the speaker treats the morning as finished.

commonMistakes.why: Last night places the event in completed past time.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Did you ever try this tool?
commonMistakes.correct: Have you ever tried this tool?
commonMistakes.why: This asks about life experience without a specified time; the present perfect is the standard taught form.

studyTips: Check whether a time marker is finished before choosing a tense.
Context can affect whether a period such as today is treated as finished.

exercises.feedback: Yesterday is a finished time reference.

exercises.prompt: I ___ this error before, so I recognize it.
exercises.feedback: Before describes experience without a particular past time.

exercises.prompt: We ___ two prototypes so far this month.
exercises.feedback: So far this month is an unfinished reporting period.

exercises.prompt: She ___ the file at 9 a.m. yesterday.
exercises.feedback: The timestamp identifies a completed past event.
Yet is typical with a negative present perfect.

exercises.prompt: ___ you ever worked with this tool?
exercises.feedback: Ever asks about experience using present perfect.

exercises.prompt: He ___ (send) the document an hour ago.
Correct the sentence: We have met the client last month.
acceptedAnswers: We met the client last month.
exercises.feedback: Last month is a completed time period.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: She never has used this interface.
acceptedAnswers: She has never used this interface.
exercises.feedback: Never usually follows have/has in this pattern.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I have bought this laptop in 2021.
exercises.feedback: A finished year makes past simple appropriate.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: We have not completed the upgrade yesterday.
acceptedAnswers: We did not complete the upgrade yesterday.
We didn't complete the upgrade yesterday.
exercises.feedback: Yesterday requires past simple in this context.
